$comment: Machine-readable inventory of the Remnant Security web estate. Prose, procedures and traps are in WEB-ESTATE.md next to this file; toolchain prerequisites and the Namecheap MCP setup are in TOOLCHAIN.md. Verified 2026-10-14 against GitHub Pages API, the Namecheap zone, and live HTTP from a second machine.

write_api.danger: Sending only the record you want to add DELETES every other record, including MX and DKIM. That takes down email. Always send the complete desired record set.

mcp_server.auth: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE (S256). No API key, no secret in any config file - the config entry is the URL only and the token lives in each CLI's own credential store.
mcp_server.token_scope: Per machine AND per CLI. Signing in on one CLI on one Mac authorises nothing else. Registration is visible in the config; authentication is not.

add_commands.claude: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user namecheap https://mcp.namecheap.com/mcp
add_commands.gemini: gemini mcp add -s user -t http namecheap https://mcp.namecheap.com/mcp
add_commands.qwen: qwen mcp add -s user -t http namecheap https://mcp.namecheap.com/mcp
add_commands.grok: grok mcp add -s user -t http namecheap https://mcp.namecheap.com/mcp

traps: codex mcp add opens a browser immediately; over SSH it hangs because the OAuth callback is on the remote machine's 127.0.0.1. Append the two-line [mcp_servers.namecheap] block to ~/.codex/config.toml instead and sign in at that machine.
grok cannot complete this OAuth flow: mcp add accepts only static --header values and there is no login subcommand. Leave it configured-but-unauthenticated; do not use grok for DNS.
Use each CLI's own mcp add. Do not hand-edit ~/.claude.json - it is over 100 KB and easy to corrupt.
mcp_server.fallback: The Namecheap web UI. Per-record editing there has no replace-all risk and is safer for a single record. The MCP buys speed, not capability.

tls.note: Every certificate in the estate is Let's Encrypt, but GitHub Pages requests and renews them automatically. There is no certbot, no ACME client and no cron job on any machine. Nothing expires that GitHub does not renew on its own.
tls.provision_trigger: Setting the Pages custom domain while the DNS record already resolves.
tls.failure_mode: If the custom domain was set BEFORE DNS existed, GitHub may never retry. The symptom is that the Pages API response has no https_certificate object at all - not a certificate in a failed state, but the field missing entirely. A healthy property shows https_certificate.state == 'approved'.
repair: wait for https_certificate.state to become 'approved' (about a minute)
tls.repair_warning: Clearing the cname deletes the CNAME file from the repo. Re-setting it recreates the file, so the round trip is safe, but do not stop halfway. Confirm the file is back before walking away.
tls.repair_observed_states: After the re-set the certificate goes NONE -> authorization_pending -> approved, usually inside a minute. Do not give up at authorization_pending.
tls.repair_transient_error: The clear/re-set pair can trigger two Pages builds seconds apart and the first may fail, leaving pages.status == 'errored' for a few minutes while the site already serves correctly. Check pages/builds: if the newest build is 'built' the error was transient. Judge by what the host actually serves, not by pages.status alone.
tls.verified_estate_wide: 2026-10-14: all 14 hostnames return 200 and all 12 Pages repos report https_enforced=true with cert=approved.

subdomain_pattern.description: Every app subdomain follows the same shape. Deviating from it is what breaks deploys.
steps: A GitHub repo named <app>-site, public (Pages custom domains need public on this plan).
A CNAME file at the repo root containing the bare hostname, no scheme and no trailing slash.
GitHub Pages enabled on main at path /.
A DNS CNAME record: host <app>, value itrimble.github.io.
https_enforced set to true AFTER GitHub provisions the certificate, which takes a few minutes.
subdomain_pattern.note: Order matters only in that the certificate cannot be issued until DNS resolves. The repo may exist first.

verification.comment: Run these from a machine other than Neo. Neo's mDNSResponder caches negative lookups for new hostnames, so curl reports 'could not resolve' long after dig succeeds.
verification.all_endpoints: for s in '' www. academy. blog. apps. lightfence. prismshift. snapdog. lectern. cybersim. plumberpuzzle. books.; do printf '%-34s %s\n' "${s}remnantsecurity.com" "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} -L --max-time 12 https://${s}remnantsecurity.com/)"; done

prerequisites.note: None of these live in the repo and none are discoverable from the code. Read TOOLCHAIN.md after relocating or cloning this folder.

required_per_property: og:image as an absolute RASTER url (png/jpeg) with width, height and alt - SVG is refused by every scraper and fails silently
seo.fonts_warning: Do not add a Google Fonts link. Fonts are self-hosted via @fontsource-variable in src/main.tsx. The removed link requested Space Grotesk, which no stylesheet references. tailwind.config.ts names it but Tailwind v4 is CSS-first here with no @config, so that file is never read.

apex_prerender.problem: The apex is a React SPA. index.html shipped an empty #root, so Bing, DuckDuckGo and the LinkedIn/Slack/Discord scrapers saw zero text.
apex_prerender.solution: Build-time SSR. npm run build = tsc -b && vite build && npm run build:ssr && npm run prerender.
apex_prerender.note: Pure Node react-dom/server. No headless browser, so CI needs nothing extra.

result.previously: 719 chars and 12 links via a noscript block, now deleted

apex_prerender.hydration: src/main.tsx hydrateRoot when #root has children, createRoot otherwise. CareerPlanSection starts from empty state and restores localStorage in an effect behind a 'restored' flag so the first client render matches the server render.
apex_prerender.build_gate: prerender.mjs exits non-zero if render() throws, returns under 20KB, or lacks <h1, the hero headline or </footer>.
apex_prerender.verified: lint 0, build 0, zero console/hydration errors, plan builder advances and resumes from localStorage across reload, headless render vs live RMSE 0

traps: og:image must be raster. SVG fails silently - the tag looks correct and the card renders blank.
A square og:image is not a large card. Scrapers crop to 1.91:1.
robots.txt matches on prefix, not path segments. Disallow: /portfolio also blocks /portfolio-labs.
In Next.js, alternates in a root layout is inherited, so every route would canonical to /. Set canonicals per page.
metadataBase falling back to localhost publishes localhost canonicals if the env var is unset in production.

A Production-only env var pinning an origin (NEXT_PUBLIC_ACADEMY_URL) outlives the domain change that made it wrong and silently overrides a correct code fallback. Prefer deleting it so the origin is written down in exactly one place.
A Vercel project listing does not show custom domains. Use list_project_domains before concluding a project does not serve a hostname.
A Vercel project with no Git connection ignores every push. Deployments with empty meta and no commit SHA were manual uploads - check that before assuming a push will deploy.
